speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what assistance has been provided to the victims of the unauthorised home address changes performed on the ICA website; and (b) what punishment will be meted out to the perpetrators who did the changes.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the procedure for a change of home address is being reviewed.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the Government will consider implementing stricter rules or guidelines to regulate the photocopying of physical NRICs to reduce the likelihood of such information being misused.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) has related questions in this Sitting and will address Mr Fahmi’s question on Singpass in its reply.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: First, let me explain the procedure for changing one’s registered address with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA).

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The fraudulent changes of address had occurred through the “Others” module in ICA’s system for electronic change of address (eCOA).

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The “Others” module had been introduced for the benefit of non-digitally savvy residents, such as the elderly or disabled.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It enables them to change their address online without having to make an in-person trip to ICA, by getting a proxy to help them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The proxy would log into the system using his or her own Singpass account and apply for a change of address for the individual by keying in the individual’s National Registration Identity Card (NRIC) number and date of issue of the NRIC.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A physical personal identification number (PIN) mailer would then be sent to the individual at his new address.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The proxy would log into the eCOA system a second time and with the PIN, complete the change of address for the individual.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In designing and building our digital services, we have to make practical trade-offs between absolute security and useability.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the case of the eCOA service, there were safeguards in place, including the need to authenticate the proxy via Singpass log-in, the use of NRIC number and date of issue of the NRIC of the person whose address was to be changed, and the use of a physical PIN mailer.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At that time, these were assessed to represent an acceptable balance between absolute security and useability.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, we now recognise that this service could be and was exploited by malicious actors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A key problem is that there was criminal action: people gave up their Singpass account to be misused.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This criminal action, which was not anticipated, was the key reason why malicious actors were able to exploit the “Others” module in the eCOA service.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They had first used Singpass accounts which had been relinquished, as proxies to initiate the change of address for another individual.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Using the date of issue of NRIC as one of the three safeguards was reasonable, but proved not adequate, as malicious actors managed to get hold of the information.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICA has since introduced an additional security feature which is face verification when individuals use their Singpass account to log into the “Myself” module of the eCOA service to change their own residential address.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This module has been resumed since 14 January 2025.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The “Others” module and the “Myself and my family” module will remain suspended until additional safeguards can be put in place.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Government places high priority on the security of our digital services from illegal and malicious actors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is both to maintain public confidence and to protect the public from harm.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We constantly test and improve the security of our systems and will continue to do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Second, let me address questions about the impact of the unauthorised changes of addresses and what assistance has been provided to the victims.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICA has reviewed all eCOA applications made through the “Others” module since October 2020, when the eCOA service was launched.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICA has ascertained that unauthorised changes took place only in the recent months, from August 2024 onwards.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICA and the Singapore Police Force (SPF) have been working with the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) and other Government agencies to mitigate the impact on these affected individuals.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICA has reached out to all 99 individuals to verify and restore the correct addresses.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICA is also assisting them to replace their physical NRIC, which will have a new date of issue.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICA is also working with other Government agencies to comprehensively assess the impact of the fraudulent change of address for the 71 individuals, in particular those whose address registered in ICA’s system had been used by other agencies to administer their schemes since the fraud began.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Agencies will provide the appropriate assistance and restoration if there has been any adverse impact on the calculation or disbursement of Government benefits, including Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers, to these individuals.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Of the 71 individuals whose addresses were successfully changed, the suspects went on to take over the Singpass accounts of 16 of the individuals.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They did so by performing a password reset for the Singpass account and requesting for a physical PIN mailer to be sent to the newly registered address.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Out of an abundance of caution, GovTech has suspended the Singpass accounts of all 99 affected individuals to prevent unauthorised activity, and has been in contact with them to reset and secure their Singpass accounts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: SPF is also coordinating with Government agencies and private entities to stop or reverse any fraudulent activity originating from the 16 compromised Singpass accounts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If there have been monetary losses arising from the compromised Singpass accounts, Police will work with agencies and financial institutions to remediate the losses wherever possible.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Third, Ms Joan Pereira asked what punishment would be meted out.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Thirteen suspects have been arrested by the Police and investigations are ongoing.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Details of the arrests and the offences for which the suspects have been charged are contained in SPF’s news releases.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: SPF will be making known other details in due course as its investigations progress further.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Exceptions apply only where required under the law, or when it is necessary to accurately identify an individual.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ICA had started investigating cases of unauthorised changes of address in September 2024.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Time was needed to investigate and triangulate information from various reports made.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: By December 2024, ICA had uncovered how the unauthorised changes of addresses were effected and what they were used for.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In parallel, ICA was also reviewing the technical aspects of improving the security of the eCOA system.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But these are judgement calls that public officers have to make every day.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is reviewing with ICA what lessons we can draw from this incident.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Upon a change of address, does the Ministry currently send letters to both the new and old addresses in order to verify that the change is genuine?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And secondly, would the Ministry consider reinstating the venue of changing residential address to be at Neighbourhood Police Posts (NPPs)?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Currently, the mailers are sent to the new address but, like I had shared in my response earlier, ICA is reviewing how this service is conducted and has instituted the use of facial verification under the "Myself" module.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, for the other modules, like "Myself and family members" as well as "Others", ICA is still reviewing what would be the best way forward in order to safeguard our electronic services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Could I ask about the second question again, please?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There have been instances in the past where there have been questions raised in this House about manpower issues that the SPF faces.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, many of our NPPs have gone towards a "man-less" operation model.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But what will happen is, if there are individuals who walk into our NPPs and ask for help to change their address, they will be guided to ICA for them to change their addresses at ICA.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now read the Orders of the Day and the Notices of Motions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
